quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #20
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When driving on gravel or dirt roads:

options.text: Your tires grip better than on pavement.
Your tires have less grip than on pavement, so you must slow down.
You can see better than on pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires have less grip than on pavement, so you must slow down.
questions.explanation: Gravel and dirt roads have less grip than pavement. You must slow down on these roads. It takes longer to stop and it is easier to skid when turning.

questions.question: Which statement about alcohol and driving is true?

options.text: If you can walk in a straight line after drinking, it is safe to drive.
If you are below the legal alcohol limit, your driving is not affected.
Alcohol affects your judgment, which you need to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol affects your judgment, which you need to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects your judgment. Good judgment is necessary to react to things you see or hear on the road. Even below the legal limit, any alcohol can hurt your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: Your license will:

options.text: Expire on your birthday.
Never expire.
Renew automatically.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expire on your birthday.
questions.explanation: Your license expires on your birthday. At least 30 days before expiration, the Division of Vehicles will mail a notice or renewal form to your home.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: You can pass from the lane next to the solid yellow line.
No one can pass from either direction.
You can pass from the lane next to the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass from the lane next to the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means traffic in the lane next to the broken line can cross to pass. Traffic in the lane next to the solid line cannot pass.

questions.question: You should not enter an intersection if you will block it when the light turns red:

options.text: Under any circumstances.
Unless you entered on a yellow light.
Unless you entered on a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under any circumstances.
questions.explanation: Even on a green light, do not enter an intersection unless you can cross completely before the light turns red. Blocking an intersection can result in a ticket.

questions.question: Use your headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days:

options.text: To keep your engine warm.
So other drivers can see your vehicle.
To warn others about bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: So other drivers can see your vehicle.
questions.explanation: On rainy, snowy, or foggy days, other drivers have trouble seeing your vehicle. Headlights make your vehicle easier to see. If you use your wipers, you must also turn on your low beam headlights.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with flashing lights is behind you. What should you do?

options.text: Drive to the right edge and slow down.
Drive to the right edge and stop.
Stay in your lane, slow down, and let it pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right edge and stop.
questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using lights and sirens. Drive to the right edge and stop until it passes. If you are in an intersection, drive through first, then stop.

questions.question: Which statement about driving speed is true?

options.text: Higher speeds increase the chance of death in a crash.
Higher speeds mean you should increase your following distance.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds increase the chance of death in a crash. At speeds over 80 miles per hour, survival is very unlikely. Speed affects how far you travel before stopping, so increase your following distance as you speed up.

questions.question: A blood alcohol level of 0.02 percent:

options.text: Does not affect your driving.
Does not put other drivers at risk.
Doubles your chance of having an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Doubles your chance of having an accident.
questions.explanation: Every 0.02 percent increase in blood alcohol nearly doubles a driver's risk of a fatal crash.

questions.question: If you see a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane:

options.text: The pedestrian must yield the right-of-way.
You must yield the right-of-way.
Honk your horn to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Blind or partially blind pedestrians carry a white cane or use a guide dog. You must give the right-of-way to a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
No U-turns.
No left turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers what traffic rules they must follow. You cannot turn right where this sign is posted.

questions.question: Which road surface freezes first?

options.text: A tunnel
An intersection
A bridge

questions.correctAnswerText: A bridge
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before other road surfaces. They freeze even when nearby roads are still dry. Bridges also thaw later than the rest of the road.

questions.question: Driving slower than other traffic is:

options.text: A good idea if the weather is bad.
Okay if you don't know the speed limit.
Often dangerous because other drivers may get frustrated and try to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often dangerous because other drivers may get frustrated and try to pass you.
questions.explanation: Driving slower than other traffic can be risky. Drivers behind you may become impatient and take unsafe risks to pass you.

questions.question: You must use your low beams whenever you drive in:

options.text: A well-lit street.
A freeway.
Fog.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fog.
questions.explanation: Use low beams when driving in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off these conditions and cause glare, making it harder to see. Fog lights can be used along with low beams if your vehicle has them.

questions.question: Should you always drive slower than other traffic?

options.text: No, driving too slowly can block traffic.
Yes, it is good defensive driving.
Yes, it is always safer.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, driving too slowly can block traffic.
questions.explanation: Drive slower during heavy traffic or bad weather. But if you drive too slowly and block normal traffic flow, you can be given a citation.

questions.question: Which of these is a common cause of traffic crashes?

options.text: Speeding and driving too fast for road conditions.
Getting enough rest and staying alert.
Watching the road and focusing on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speeding and driving too fast for road conditions.
questions.explanation: Speeding above the limit, driving too slowly, and driving too fast for conditions all cause crashes. Always drive with traffic flow and obey speed limits.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Drive only in the direction shown by the arrow.
Curve ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive only in the direction shown by the arrow.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers what they must do. You must drive in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: You want to pass a motorcycle. You must:

options.text: Stay in the right lane because the motorcycle is small and doesn't use all of the lane.
Honk your horn to make the motorcycle move to the shoulder.
Move your whole vehicle into the left lane before and during the pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your whole vehicle into the left lane before and during the pass.
questions.explanation: Give a motorcycle a full lane when passing. Never share the same lane as a motorcycle. If you move back too soon, you could force the rider to swerve right into traffic or off the road.

questions.question: A broken yellow line between two lanes means:

options.text: Both lanes are going the same direction.
You can pass when it is safe.
You cannot pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Dashed yellow lines separate lanes going in opposite directions. You can pass if there is no oncoming traffic in the passing lane.

questions.question: Allow extra space in front of your vehicle when following a:

options.text: Station wagon.
Passenger car.
Motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Give extra space when driving behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop faster than other vehicles, and you need room to stop if the rider brakes or falls. Also, motorcycles are hard to see at night because they have only one tail light.

questions.question: What blocks the smooth flow of traffic?

options.text: Slowing down to look at a crash.
Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.
Using public transportation instead of driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down to look at a crash.
questions.explanation: Slowing down to look at crashes causes traffic jams and should be avoided.

questions.question: Slowing down to look at crashes or unusual things:

options.text: Causes traffic jams.
Prevents rear-end crashes.
Improves traffic flow by preventing crashes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Causes traffic jams.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down to look at crashes or unusual things. This causes traffic jams.

questions.question: A broken yellow line down the center of a road means:

options.text: A construction zone is ahead.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means any driver can pass when no traffic is coming toward them.

questions.question: You can identify an aggressive driver by:

options.text: Sudden and unsafe lane changes.
How many passengers are in their car.
Driving slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sudden and unsafe lane changes.
questions.explanation: Watch other drivers while driving. If you see an aggressive driver making sudden or unsafe lane changes, do not challenge them. Stay away from them.

questions.question: To avoid skidding on slippery surfaces, you should:

options.text: Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.
Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.
Slow down before entering curves and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
questions.explanation: Slow down before you enter a curve. Braking on a curve can cause you to skid.
